A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same language-conditioned depth-estimation research, renamed from PriorDiffusion to Iris. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v3 reports original depth-estimation experiments, convergence comparisons, small-region evaluations, prompt ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and reports additional backbone comparisons, DIODE evaluations, text-stage controls and caption-count ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same text-integration mechanism: frozen CLIP text embeddings and VAE image/depth representations condition the diffusion model, with unchanged diffusion equations, loss and inference recurrence. The additional backbone experiments apply this conditioning strategy without introducing a new integration component.

E1.justification: v4 adds DIODE as a fifth real-world zero-shot depth benchmark. Hypersim and Virtual KITTI training coverage and the NYUv2, KITTI, ETH3D and ScanNet evaluations remain. This extends dataset coverage within the existing monocular depth task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated Lotus-D, Lotus-G and E2E-FT baselines, including reported and retrained results; these methods were only discussed in v3. HDN, DiverseDepth, LeReS and MiDaS disappear from the quantitative comparison. Appendix Table 3 also adds a Marigold comparator to the prompt ablation.

E3.justification: The new Lotus and E2E-FT experiments introduce 20,000-iteration training and one-step inference configurations, with backbone-specific sample counts, resolutions, normalization and caption generators. Text-stage and caption-count controls expand the evaluation design. v4's main text changes the reported default from ten sampled training captions to one, although Appendix B.2 still describes ten for Marigold, leaving that default inconsistently documented.

E4.justification: Table 1 expands text-availability analysis to training-only, inference-only and joint conditioning across several backbones; v3 already tested missing inference text for its own model. New Table 6 evaluates one, two, five and ten training captions. Figure 9 adds the correct-text prediction beside the incorrect-text failure. Existing small-area, prompt, denoising-step and iterative-refinement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests for its experimental results. v4's proposed future uncertainty-based language filtering is not implemented statistical reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive Lotus/E2E-FT, text-stage and DIODE results, including DIODE δ1/AbsRel of 78.9/29.8 for Marigold with text. Table 6 adds two- and five-caption outcomes. Many Marigold scores are retained or redistributed: v4's default matches v3's one-caption prompt-ablation results, while the earlier ten-caption scores remain in Table 6. The small-area and denoising-step tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, conditioning variables, training loss, inference update and appendix alignment/metric definitions remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The expanded conditional-distribution explanation is qualitative rather than a new derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: v3 presents PriorDiffusion as a novel model and claims state-of-the-art zero-shot performance. v4 presents Iris as an investigation of text integration across Marigold, Lotus and E2E-FT, claiming generally improved baseline-relative accuracy. It also explicitly claims occasional benefits from text used at only one stage and promotes the existing iterative-refinement observation into a central finding.

C2.justification: v4 adds distinct explanations for training-only benefits through learned disambiguation and inference-only benefits through pretrained text associations. It interprets caption-count saturation as redundancy in geometric information. The discussion emphasizes conditioning that reduces possible 3D solutions and proposes consistency filtering or uncertainty estimation for inaccurate descriptions, extending the earlier geometric-prior and attention-based interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds detailed Lotus and E2E-FT configurations, including GPU counts, batch accumulation, optimizers, schedules, precision, preprocessing, dataset mixing and InternVL3 captions with a 77-token limit. Existing Marigold details largely remain. The release promise expands from code to code and generated text data, but neither PDF establishes an available release. Caption-count documentation remains inconsistent.

R1.justification: The work shifts from claiming the first language-prior approach for diffusion-based 3D perception to investigating an insufficiently studied capability of existing depth estimators. This substantially changes its novelty positioning. References add Jasmine, InternVL3, DIODE, ETA, ProtoDepth and HOMER, while removing the LLaVA-generated-prompts paper, ExpansionNet v2 and the MaskDINO reference.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements and conclusion are extensively rewritten around Iris and an empirical investigation. 'Our contributions' becomes 'Our findings,' Method becomes Formulation, implementation detail shifts toward the appendix, and appendix training and caption sections are expanded and reorganized. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond renaming.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned into backbone-specific comparison blocks with DIODE columns, text-stage variants, highlighting and gray styling for results the authors could not reproduce. Table 6 is added, Figure 9 gains a correct-text comparison panel, and several figures and appendix tables move. Most qualitative image panels are retained. Figure 7's former NYUv2 panel is incorrectly relabeled KITTI in v4.

improvement.justification: v3's broad language-benefit claims rely chiefly on one Marigold-based system. v4 substantially strengthens their empirical foundation through paired baseline/text-enabled evaluations across several estimators, text-stage controls and caption-count analysis, while replacing broad state-of-the-art framing with more measured claims. Caption-count inconsistencies, missing DIODE protocol details and the Figure 7 labeling error limit reproducibility and presentation, but the stronger evidence for generality and clearer contribution scope provide a substantial net improvement.
